literal: Meanwhile the usher Zhang Sining, blunt and unyielding in speech, died a heroic death in the hostel.
idiomatic: The usher Zhang Sining spoke bluntly and died heroically in the hostel.

literal: When Chang returned, Emperor Xiaowen rebuked him: "The protocol of bearing commission permits death but not dishonor; even exiled to the sea's edge one ought to hold integrity until death.
idiomatic: Chang returned, and Xiaowen rebuked him: "An envoy may die but must not be shamed; exiled to the sea's edge, he should still die holding his integrity."

literal: You could not tie your hair and present your head bound—a thing already hateful.
idiomatic: You would not even bind your hair and offer your head—that was hateful enough.

literal: Instead you bowed your brows and pecked at food like a dog or horse.
idiomatic: Then you bowed and ate like a dog or horse.

literal: Life must end in death; how long or short is it?
idiomatic: All who live must die; how long does it matter?

literal: Had you died to achieve a name and left it in bamboo and silk, how would that compare to willingly eating fodder and shaming lord and father?
idiomatic: Had you died for a name in the histories, how would that compare to eating fodder and shaming your lord and father?

literal: Even if you cannot be ashamed before Su Wu from afar, can you not be ashamed before Sining nearby!
idiomatic: If you cannot match Su Wu from afar, can you not be ashamed before Sining beside you!

literal: He was then dismissed from office.
idiomatic: He was dismissed.

literal: At the beginning of the Jingming era he was appointed Vice Director of the Palace Secretariat, promoted to Supervisor of Attendants of the Yellow Gate, Grand Rectifier of the province, Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary, and concurrently Director of the Masters of Writing.
idiomatic: In early Jingming he became Vice Director of the Secretariat, then Yellow Gate Supervisor, provincial rectifier, regular attendant, and concurrent Director of the Masters of Writing.

literal: At that time Luoyang County captured a white rat.
idiomatic: Luoyang County then caught a white rat.

literal: Chang memorialized, holding that according to the canon of auspicious omens, when frontier governors and prefectural officials of two thousand bushels do not respect imperial orders but are harsh and violent and the people groan, white rats appear.
idiomatic: Chang memorialized that the canon of auspicious omens says white rats appear when frontier governors and two-thousand-bushel magistrates defy orders, act brutally, and the people groan.

literal: He thereupon set forth current affairs, mostly admonitions.
idiomatic: He then addressed current affairs, mostly in admonition.

literal: An edict praised his intent.
idiomatic: An edict praised his meaning.

literal: He was transferred to Palace Attendant and concurrently Minister of Personnel, soon made regular minister while still Palace Attendant.
idiomatic: He became Palace Attendant and concurrent Minister of Personnel, soon regular minister while still attendant.

literal: Chang merely held his post without stirring anyone up; with Palace Attendant Yuan Hui and others he formed a clique, was favored by Emperor Xuanwu, and men of the time despised him.
idiomatic: Chang only kept his post without stirring things up; he and Attendant Yuan Hui cliqued together, won Xuanwu's favor, and contemporaries despised them.

literal: He went out as Governor of Xuzhou.
idiomatic: He was sent out as Governor of Xuzhou.

literal: Chang was a Confucian by origin and naturally lacked military grasp; moreover Yang Sheo's son Xie served as Chang's Major, monopolizing military affairs and blocking Chang's eyes and ears, and officers resented it.
idiomatic: Chang was a scholar by birth and knew little of war; Yang Sheo's son Xie was his major, monopolized military affairs, kept Chang in the dark, and the troops resented it.

literal: Fu Wenyi, garrison chief of Mount Xiong, exhausted grain and firewood and surrendered the city to Liang.
idiomatic: Fu Wenyi, garrison chief at Mount Xiong, ran out of grain and fuel and surrendered the city to Liang.

literal: When Chang saw the city surrender he fled first in retreat, and the armies in succession broke and ran.
idiomatic: Seeing the surrender, Chang fled first; the armies then broke and ran.

literal: A great cold struck; soldiers who froze to death or lost hands and feet were more than half.
idiomatic: In bitter cold more than half the men froze to death or lost hands and feet.

literal: Since Wei began strategy on the south bank of the Yangtze, only Prince of Zhongshan Ying was defeated at Zhongli; Chang's setback at Mount Xiong was the severest.
idiomatic: Since Wei began campaigning south of the Yangtze, only Prince of Zhongshan Ying had lost at Zhongli; Chang's defeat at Mount Xiong was worse.

literal: Emperor Xuanwu sent Yellow Gate Attendant Zhen Chen post-haste to bind Chang and probe his defeat; an edict ordered dismissal from office.
idiomatic: Xuanwu sent Yellow Gate Attendant Zhen Chen by post relay to bind Chang and investigate the defeat; an edict stripped him of office.

literal: From other commanders and leaders downward, all were permitted restoration by amnesty.
idiomatic: Other commanders and leaders were all allowed restoration by amnesty.

literal: Before long he was appointed Minister of Ceremonies, then made Governor of Yong Province, advanced to Defender-General of the West, with addition as Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary.
idiomatic: Soon he was Minister of Ceremonies, then Governor of Yong, Defender-General of the West, and regular attendant.

literal: He died in office; posthumous title Mu.
idiomatic: He died in office; posthumous title Mu.

literal: Chang was lenient and forbearing in pity, skilled at soothing.
idiomatic: Chang was gentle, forgiving, and skilled at soothing people.

literal: At Xuzhou, when garrison soldiers fell ill he personally inspected them; when frontier troops whose term expired did not return, he allowed them to fill later labor—throughout Chang's tenure they only then returned, and the populace praised him.
idiomatic: At Xuzhou he personally tended sick garrison troops; when frontier men whose terms had expired did not return, he let them serve later terms—only after his tenure ended did they go home, and the people praised him.

literal: His son Yuan Yu, styled Zhongxun, had no other talent.
idiomatic: His son Yuan Yu, styled Zhongxun, had no other ability.

literal: He married Emperor Xiaowen's daughter the Princess of Yiyang, was appointed Commandant of Horse Caparisons.
idiomatic: He married Xiaowen's daughter Princess Yiyang and became Commandant of Horse Caparisons.

literal: Posts as Grand Marshal's Major, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
idiomatic: He held posts as Grand Marshal's major and grand master of splendid happiness.

literal: He died; enfeoffed as Director of the Palace Secretariat posthumously.
idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made Director of the Secretariat.

literal: His son Shi Sheng, aide to the Grand Minister with protocol equal to the Three Excellencies opening a mansion.
idiomatic: His son Shi Sheng was aide to a minister with protocol equal to the Three Excellencies.

literal: Yuan Yu's fifth younger brother Yuan Ming, styled Youzhang.
idiomatic: Yuan Yu's fifth brother Yuan Ming, styled Youzhang.

literal: He ranged through many books and also had literary skill; his bearing was leisurely and moist, his advances and retreats admirable.
idiomatic: He read widely and wrote well; his manner was easy and polished, his bearing admirable.

literal: At the beginning of Yong'an he long served concurrently as Director of the Masters of Writing and was cherished by Prince of Linhuai Wang Yu.
idiomatic: At the start of Yong'an he long served as concurrent Director of the Masters of Writing and was cherished by Prince of Linhuai Wang Yu.

literal: When Yu opened a staff he was brought in as concurrent aide and still led a personal detachment.
idiomatic: When Yu opened a staff he became concurrent aide and still led his own troops.

literal: When Emperor Xiaowu ascended the throne he served as Lang performing ceremonies and was enfeoffed Baron of Chengyang, promoted to Vice Director of the Palace Secretariat.
idiomatic: When Xiaowu ascended the throne he performed ceremonial duties as Lang, was enfeoffed Baron of Chengyang, and promoted to Vice Director of the Secretariat.

literal: At the end of Yongxi he lived on Mount Gou east of Luoyang and wrote his "Rhapsody on Secluded Dwelling."
idiomatic: At the end of Yongxi he lived on Mount Gou east of Luoyang and wrote his Rhapsody on Secluded Dwelling.

literal: At the time Yuan Ming's friend Wang You lived in Yingchuan; suddenly he dreamed You came with wine to speak farewell and presented a poem as gift.
idiomatic: Yuan Ming's friend Wang You was in Yingchuan; suddenly You dreamed Wang came with wine to say farewell and left a parting poem.

literal: When day broke he recalled the poem's ten characters: "From this day when I go forth / the markets and courts I shall visit no more."
idiomatic: At dawn he recalled ten lines: "From this day I go—/ no more the markets and courts."

literal: Yuan Ming sighed: "You by nature did not linger with the vulgar; lodging a while among men—and now this dream, and the poem too—surely there is another cause."
idiomatic: Yuan Ming sighed: "You never kept company with the vulgar; you only lodged among men—and now this dream and poem. Something else must be at hand."

literal: After three days he indeed heard You was killed by mutinous troops.
idiomatic: Three days later he learned You had been killed by mutinous troops.

literal: Searching the date of his death, it was the very night the dream came.
idiomatic: The date of his death was the night of the dream.

literal: In the Tianping era he concurrently served as Director in the Ministry of Personnel and assisted Li Xie on an embassy to Liang; Southerners praised him.
idiomatic: In Tianping he served concurrently as director in the Ministry of Personnel and assisted Li Xie's embassy to Liang; Southerners praised him.

literal: On return he was appointed Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, transferred to Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary, and supervised the diarists.
idiomatic: On return he became Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, then regular attendant supervising the diarists.

literal: He accumulated years in the historiography office and paid no mind to it at all.
idiomatic: He spent years in the historiography office and paid it no heed.

literal: Also concurrently Yellow Gate Attendant and Grand Rectifier of the province.
idiomatic: He also held Yellow Gate Attendant and provincial rectifier concurrently.

literal: Yuan Ming knew how to set himself apart; he did not socialize idly, drinking wine and composing poetry—when inspiration came he forgot to return.
idiomatic: Yuan Ming held himself apart; he did not socialize lightly, but drank and wrote poetry and forgot to return when inspiration took him.

literal: He loved arcane reasoning and wrote several tens of essays on history, masters, and miscellaneous topics; his other writings are collected separately.
idiomatic: He loved metaphysics and wrote dozens of essays on history, masters, and miscellany; other works are collected elsewhere.

literal: In youth when returning from his district to Luoyang, on the road he met the Governor of Xiangzhou, Prince of Zhongshan Xi.
idiomatic: As a youth returning from his district to Luoyang, he met on the road Xiangzhou Governor Prince of Zhongshan Xi.

literal: Xi, a man of broad knowledge, saw him and exclaimed: "Young Master Lu has such spirit—he need only recite the 'Encountering Sorrow,' drink fine wine, and is himself a fine vessel."
idiomatic: Xi, a learned man, saw him and exclaimed: "Young Master Lu has such spirit—he need only recite the Encountering Sorrow, drink good wine, and he is a vessel fit for use."

literal: He kept him several days and gave silk and a horse on parting.
idiomatic: He kept him several days and on parting gave silk and a horse.

literal: Yuan Ming married three times in all; his second wife the Lady Zheng had improper relations with Yuan Ming's elder brother's son Shi Qi, and Yuan Ming could not cut her off.
idiomatic: Yuan Ming married three times; his second wife Lady Zheng had relations with his elder brother's son Shi Qi, and Yuan Ming could not sever her.

literal: He also liked to boast of his family's standing; opinion of the time depreciated him for this.
idiomatic: He also boasted of his family's standing, for which contemporaries looked down on him.

literal: Yuan Ming's younger brother Yuan Ji, styled Youxu, was brutal and fond of wine; once at his wife's clan drinking, over a slight offense he cut down a guest.
idiomatic: Yuan Ming's brother Yuan Ji, styled Youxu, was brutal and fond of wine; once at his wife's kin he killed a guest over a slight.

literal: Post: General Who Assists the State, Grand Marshal's Major; posthumously enfeoffed General-in-Chief of Fast Cavalry, Minister of Personnel, Governor of Youzhou; posthumous title Xuan.
idiomatic: He reached General Who Assists the State and Grand Marshal's major; posthumously he was made General-in-Chief of Fast Cavalry, Minister of Personnel, Governor of Youzhou, posthumous title Xuan.

literal: Chang's younger brother Shangzhi, styled Jiru, childhood name Xianxia.
idiomatic: Chang's brother Shangzhi, styled Jiru, childhood name Xianxia.

literal: He too was valued for Confucian purity, posts: Left Chief Clerk of the Grand Marshal, General of the Vanguard, Governor of Jizhou, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
idiomatic: He too was valued for scholarly purity and reached left chief clerk of the Grand Marshal, vanguard general, Governor of Jizhou, and grand master of splendid happiness.

literal: His eldest son Wenfu, styled Yuanyou, ranged through literature and history and had reputation in the time.
idiomatic: His eldest son Wenfu, styled Yuanyou, ranged through literature and history and was renowned.

literal: Post: Aide in the Secretariat of the Minister of Works.
idiomatic: He was aide in the Minister of Works' secretariat.

literal: Wenfu's younger brother Wenyi, styled Zhongyou, was very impetuous in youth and in later years much reformed.
idiomatic: Wenfu's brother Wenyi, styled Zhongyou, was very rash in youth but reformed much in later years.

literal: For military merit he was enfeoffed Baron of Fanyang and made Grand Masters of Palace Counsel.
idiomatic: For military merit he was enfeoffed Baron of Fanyang and made grand master of palace counsel.

literal: Wenyi's younger brother Wenfu, styled Shuwei, was open and direct by nature, post: Regular Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary attached to the Secretariat.
idiomatic: Wenyi's brother Wenfu, styled Shuwei, was frank by nature and reached regular cavalier attendant attached to the secretariat.

literal: His son Qian.
idiomatic: His son was Qian.

literal: Qian's appearance was striking and he spoke well; in youth he had the ambition of a grown man; he rose repeatedly to Military Service Aide in the Grand General's office, was forceful and capable in affairs, known to Wen Xiang, who said he would ultimately be greatly useful.
idiomatic: Qian was striking in appearance and eloquent; in youth he had a man's ambition; he rose to military service aide in the grand general's office, was forceful in affairs, and Wen Xiang said he would prove greatly useful.

literal: Wang Sizheng was captured at Yingchuan; Wen Xiang treasured his talent.
idiomatic: Wang Sizheng was captured at Yingchuan; Wen Xiang prized his talent.

literal: Qian calmly told Wen Xiang: "Sizheng could not die holding integrity—how is he worth prizing?"
idiomatic: Qian calmly told Wen Xiang: "Sizheng could not die holding his integrity—why prize him?"

literal: Wen Xiang said to those around him: "With Lu Qian I have gained another Wang Sizheng."
idiomatic: Wen Xiang told his attendants: "With Lu Qian I have gained another Wang Sizheng."

literal: In the Tianbao era he was appointed Director of the Left Household Bureau.
idiomatic: In Tianbao he was appointed director of the left household bureau.

literal: For criticizing the Wei History he was, with Wang Songnian, Li Shu and others, all placed under prohibition.
idiomatic: For criticizing the Wei History he was, with Wang Songnian and Li Shu, placed under prohibition.

literal: When Prince of Qinghe Wang Yue rescued Jiangling, Qian alone was specially pardoned as Yue's mobile staff secretary.
idiomatic: When Prince of Qinghe Wang Yue rescued Jiangling, Qian alone was specially pardoned to serve on Yue's mobile staff.

literal: On return he passed through Vice Director of Secretariat and Yellow Gate Attendant.
idiomatic: On return he served as vice director of the secretariat and yellow gate attendant.

literal: A slave falsely accused him of plotting rebellion; Emperor Wenxuan clarified the matter and handed the slave over to Qian, who did not punish him.
idiomatic: A slave falsely accused him of rebellion; Wenxuan cleared him and gave the slave to Qian, who did not punish him.

literal: Yellow Gate Attendant Zheng Zimo memorialized that when Qian followed Prince of Qinghe Wang Yue on the southern campaign, Yue had Qian persuade Liang general Hou Tian, who greatly accepted bribes from Tian, and on return did not report it.
idiomatic: Yellow Gate Attendant Zheng Zimo memorialized that on the southern campaign with Prince of Qinghe Wang Yue, Yue had Qian persuade Liang general Hou Tian; Qian took large bribes from Tian and did not report it on return.

literal: Emperor Wenxuan gave Qian a hundred blows with the rod and still cut off his beard; Qian's color did not change.
idiomatic: Wenxuan had Qian beaten a hundred strokes and cut off his beard; Qian's face did not change.

literal: He served as Vice Director of the Luoyang Prefecture, Administrator of Huai Province, Governor of Jiangzhou—wherever he went there was good government.
idiomatic: He served as vice director of Luoyang prefecture, administrator of Huai, and governor of Jiang—wherever he went his rule was good.

literal: When Emperor Xiaozhao became Chancellor, Qian was made Left Aide of the mobile staff on the Yangzhou circuit.
idiomatic: When Xiaozhao became chancellor, Qian was made left aide of the Yangzhou mobile staff.

literal: Earlier Liang general Wang Lin had brought his lord Xiao Zhuang to Shouyang; the court made Lin Governor of Yangzhou and ordered Qian with Lin as southern campaign strategist.
idiomatic: Earlier Liang general Wang Lin had brought his lord Xiao Zhuang to Shouyang; the court made Lin governor of Yangzhou and ordered Qian to strategize the southern campaign with him.

literal: Later appointed Mobile Staff Director of Masters of Writing and Peer with protocol equal to Three Excellencies.
idiomatic: Later he was made mobile staff director of the masters of writing with protocol equal to the Three Excellencies.

literal: Wang Lin was bent on plans south; Qian held the times not yet ripe, hence he and Lin had a rift and repeatedly memorialized against each other.
idiomatic: Wang Lin was bent on advancing south; Qian held the time not ripe, so they quarreled and repeatedly memorialized against each other.

literal: Emperor Wucheng recalled Lin to Ye and appointed Qian Governor of Yangzhou, holding concurrent Mobile Staff Director.
idiomatic: Wucheng recalled Lin to Ye and made Qian governor of Yangzhou, concurrently mobile staff director.

literal: Qian was in Huainan thirteen years and planted great achievements; Chen men feared him.
idiomatic: Qian spent thirteen years in Huainan and built a great record; the Chen feared him.

literal: The Chen ruler wrote his frontier generals: "Lu Qian is still there—you should prepare deeply."
idiomatic: The Chen ruler wrote his frontier generals: "Lu Qian is still there—you must prepare deeply."

literal: When Emperor Wenxuan first pacified Huainan, tax relief was granted ten years; when the term expired, by the Tiantong and Wuping eras levies were rather mixed.
idiomatic: When Wenxuan first pacified Huainan, tax relief was granted for ten years; after it expired, under Tiantong and Wuping levies grew tangled.

literal: Moreover Gao Yuanhai held power and cut off fishing and hunting; households had no way to support themselves.
idiomatic: Moreover Gao Yuanhai held power and banned fishing and hunting, so households could not support themselves.

literal: Various merchant Hu with state debt interest, eunuch Chen Dexin indulged their reckless entries against rich Huainan families and had prefectures and counties collect debts.
idiomatic: Merchant Hu owed the state interest; eunuch Chen Dexin let them post reckless claims against rich Huainan families and had prefectures collect.

literal: Also an edict sent several thousand Turkish horses within Yangzhou's jurisdiction and ordered local magnates to buy them at high price—the money only just entered.
idiomatic: An edict also sent several thousand Turkish horses into Yangzhou and ordered local magnates to buy them dear—the money had barely entered.

literal: Then came an edict to round up horses between the Jiang and Huai and send them to the government stables.
idiomatic: Then came an edict to round up horses between the Jiang and Huai and send them to government stables.

literal: Hence the people were disturbed and gnashed teeth in lament.
idiomatic: The people were in turmoil and gnashed their teeth in rage.

literal: Qian soothed affairs as they arose and also exercised expedients, so there was calm.
idiomatic: Qian soothed matters as they arose and used expedients, so the region grew calm.

literal: In the third year of Wuping he was recalled as Director of the Five Armies Bureau.
idiomatic: In the third year of Wuping he was recalled as director of the five armies bureau.

literal: Yangzhou clerks and people, because Qian had abstained from wine and meat and devoutly believed in Buddhism, held great Buddhist assemblies and with incense and flowers lined the road weeping to send him off.
idiomatic: Yangzhou clerks and people, because Qian abstained from wine and meat and devoutly believed in Buddhism, held great assemblies and with incense and flowers lined the road weeping to send him off.

literal: Qian sighed: "I fear before long I shall come again!"
idiomatic: Qian sighed: "I fear I shall soon be back!"

literal: At Ye not long after, he was again made Mobile Staff Director on the Yangzhou circuit.
idiomatic: At Ye, before long, he was again made mobile staff director on the Yangzhou circuit.

literal: In the fourth year Chen general Wu Mingche came to raid; the army commander Feng Fuxiang went to rescue.
idiomatic: In the fourth year Chen general Wu Mingche raided; army commander Feng Fuxiang went to rescue.

literal: Chen troops reached Xian; Fuxiang would not follow; Qian argued firmly in vain, worried and angry fell ill, lay under the tent, and was indeed defeated.
idiomatic: Chen troops reached Xian; Fuxiang would not follow; Qian argued in vain, fell ill with worry and anger, lay under the tent, and defeat followed.

literal: Chen men then besieged Shouyang, dammed the Shao Pond, and flooded it with water.
idiomatic: The Chen then besieged Shouyang, dammed the Shao Pond, and flooded the city.

literal: An edict made Wang Changchun southern campaign commander-in-chief.
idiomatic: An edict appointed Wang Changchun commander-in-chief of the southern campaign.

literal: Changchun's army halted south of the river, much issuing grain to soldiers, then sounded horns intending to withdraw yet selling rice cheap;
idiomatic: Changchun's army halted south of the river, issued much grain to the troops, then sounded horns to withdraw while selling rice cheap;

literal: When encamped he sold rice dear again.
idiomatic: When he encamped he sold rice dear again.
